# HTMLP 0.3

Statically enforceable token limits for context files. A strict prompt file format and a matching Rust API.

Current release: v0.3.0-alpha.1. Distributed through GitHub, not crates.io.
CLI: cargo install --git https://github.com/alexmckenley/htmlp --tag v0.3.0-alpha.1 --features cli
Rust: htmlp = { git = "https://github.com/alexmckenley/htmlp", tag = "v0.3.0-alpha.1" }
Add tokens for Cl100k, json for serialization, schema for the document JSON Schema.

Save as .htmlp:
<htmlp max-tokens="1k" reason="Shared context.">
<workflow id="routine">Make one change. Test it.</workflow>
</htmlp>

Sign intentional budgets: htmlp sign ./prompts
Check: htmlp check ./prompts
One htmlp root per file. Every other element name is author-chosen.
Names are lowercase ASCII letters, digits, hyphens; must start with a letter; htmlp is reserved.
Names are open, attributes are closed: id, max-tokens, per-item, reason, sig. Unknown attribute = error.
A name carries no role, message kind, or trust meaning. HTMLP defines no vocabulary.
id is optional and unique per file. Name = kind, id = identity; several elements may share a name.
Every declared max-tokens or per-item requires a nonblank reason on that element.
sig hashes local limits and reason; check rejects missing/stale signatures.
Content edits do not need re-signing. Do not automatically sign in CI.
Signatures are checksums, not approvals; editors can re-sign unchanged reasons.
Each file is independent; no external configuration or directory inheritance.
1k = 1000 tokens. Default encoding: cl100k_base, not a universal model tokenizer.
max-tokens bounds an element's whole subtree; per-item caps each direct child element.
Variables use {{name}}, with no limits or attributes; names cannot collide with ids.
Repeated variable names reuse a binding. Empty elements may self-close.
Escape literal < and & in Markdown. Write &#123;&#123;name}} for a literal {{name}}. Unknown markup fails.
Static checks defer variable-dependent budgets (tokens: null, deferred: true).
render substitutes literal bindings and checks final file, element, and per-item budgets.
Inline limits and reasons are editable; policy changes need review.

Rust: markup and the API build the same tree. Element is the primitive in both.
Element::new(name) with .id, .text, .variable, .template, .element, .max_tokens, .per_item.
Setting a budget clears its signature; call Document::sign() to accept in-memory budgets.
Document::new(max_tokens, reason, children), .element(child), .elements(), .elements_by_name(name).
.template(source) and parse_template(source) parse {{name}} through the markup text path.
Same nodes as markup, differing only in source positions. .text() is literal; templates do not decode entities.
document.render(&bindings, &counter), equivalently render_checked(&document, &bindings, &counter).
Returns RenderedDocument only after full validation; no partial output, no way to fabricate it.
text(), into_text(), measurement(), element(id), elements_by_name(name), elements(), spans(), report().
ElementOrigin has name, path (child indices from root), optional id, position; anonymous elements stay identifiable.
Element ranges nest and may overlap; spans() partitions the text once. Do not sum parent and child measurements.
parse/parse_file check syntax; lint checks static budgets; render enforces final budgets.
to_string() is an unchecked text view showing unbound variables as {{name}}.
TokenCounter trait: name() and count(text); lint requires a name matching the document tokenizer.

HTMLP validates structure and budgets; the application owns meaning.
No roles, message kinds, tool identity, request settings, or usage accounting in HTMLP.
0.3 removed the 0.2 runtime feature (ContentSource, Role, PromptFragment, ModelRequest, TokenUsage).
Define those categories in your own types and pair them with checked render output.
An element named system-prompt is a label for readers and elements_by_name, never a provider role.
